angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 811,186 km at 13.90 pc = 0.78 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Boyajian et al. (2012), ApJ 746, 101, HD 146233: the Hipparcos parallax the radius was computed with (van Leeuwen 2007), 71.93 +/- 0.37 mas, inverted (https://doi.org/10.1088/0004-637X/746/1/101): 13.902 +/- 0.072 pc; Gaia DR3 parallax 70.7371 +/- 0.0631 mas (same row, RUWE 0.98), 1120.6 standard errors, is not used
radiusSource: Radius 1.166 +/- 0.026 solar radii from Boyajian et al. (2012), ApJ 746, 101, HD 146233: radius in solar radii, from the limb-darkened angular diameter 0.78 +/- 0.017 mas (CHARA) and the Hipparcos parallax, 1.166 +/- 0.026 (https://doi.org/10.1088/0004-637X/746/1/101): 811,186 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.887 +/- 0.019 solar masses from Boyajian et al. (2012), ApJ 746, 101, HD 146233: mass in solar masses, from Yonsei-Yale isochrones at the measured radius and temperature (a model value), 0.887 +/- 0.019 (https://doi.org/10.1088/0004-637X/746/1/101); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 5433 +/- 69 K from Boyajian et al. (2012), ApJ 746, 101, HD 146233: effective temperature in K, from the angular diameter and the bolometric flux, 5433 +/- 69 (https://doi.org/10.1088/0004-637X/746/1/101). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Boyajian et al. (2012), ApJ 746, 101, HD 146233: effective temperature in K, from the angular diameter and the bolometric flux, 5433 +/- 69 (https://doi.org/10.1088/0004-637X/746/1/101)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/hd-146233.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.253, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
